idiom_name: RuboCop layout cops (two-space indent, end alignment) plus Style/GuardClause
implementation_notes: Ruby blocks close with end or a brace, so the rectangle depends on end alignment and a two-space step; the community style guide and RuboCop's Layout department make that mechanical, while Style/GuardClause and Layout/EmptyLineAfterGuardClause encode the depth half - the guide shows the nested-if version next to its flat guard-clause replacement. What replaces the classic structure: modifier forms such as 'return unless valid?' collapse a one-level guard into one line, and Layout/EndAlignment keeps the closing end in the rectangle's bottom-right corner. The hand form is justified in codebases that never adopted RuboCop; there, follow the existing indentation.
code_sketch:
def apply(account, amount)
  return if amount.zero?                 # guard clause: the body stays flat
  raise ArgumentError, "negative" if amount.negative?

  account.balance += amount
  account.touch                          # one level, one end at the bottom
end
pitfalls: Modifier-if reads well for a single statement but hides logic when the condition grows; Style/GuardClause and Metrics/BlockNesting thresholds have to be configured together or they contradict each other.
do...end versus braces changes precedence and layout - a multi-line brace block passed as an argument breaks the rectangle - so pick one per project and let Style/BlockDelimiters enforce it.
RuboCop autocorrection rewrites whole files; run it as its own commit or behaviour diffs drown in formatting noise.
